**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve unknown outcomes for ambiguous scan-state writes**

If the Store commits a cursor-and-retained-items PUT but loses its response, the durable positions have advanced, contrary to this clause's guarantee that an ambiguously failed write leaves the earlier positions. Document A's INV-A2/A3/A5 explicitly distinguish applied, not-applied and unknown outcomes; treating ambiguity as non-application can cause already-committed units and retained items to be processed again. Defer ambiguous outcomes to A's recovery procedure, restrict the earlier-position guarantee to confirmed non-application, and give FC-55 separate applied-response-lost and unapplied variants.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound chunk reopening by the open-unit capacity**

When `CHUNK_SIZE > OPEN_UNITS_CAP`, a revision behind the cursor causes this rule to reopen an entire chunk and immediately exceed SC-8's hard open-unit bound. D-5 exposes these as independent parameters without prohibiting that configuration, and SC-4 only limits frontier advancement, not reopening behind the cursor. This also undermines the bounded growth used to size the admission reserve. Specify capacity-aware, resumable reopening or require a compatible configuration, and exercise the boundary in FC-54/FC-57.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck deadlines after external work consumes time**

If a task is unexpired during the initial sweep but its deadline passes during a failing fetch or retry sleep, the specified ordering provides no subsequent deadline sweep before exit-and-resume. BUD-1 bounds calls by the execution budget rather than the task deadline, so following these rules can defer escalation until another execution, contradicting FC-51's explicit requirement to escalate in the same run when the deadline passes mid-run. Require deadline re-evaluation after calls and before retries, waits and budget exits, with escalation time preserved.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep task-scoped quota deferrals from ending reconciliation**

Under the explicitly permitted per-task D-7 scope, a task receiving a 429 with a wait longer than the remaining budget makes this rule terminate the entire run, even when other admitted tasks have eligible work and usable execution time remains. That directly contradicts INV-F4's requirement to record a task's rate limit and continue with the next task; repeated throttling of the first task can starve later reconciliation. Persist the affected scope's `not_before` and continue independent work, reserving whole-run termination for actual budget exhaustion or the absence of eligible work, and add a multi-task quota case alongside FC-12.
